text:
Oh, how I adore you! with the light of day

I invoke your name, impassioned and sad,

and when the sky dresses itself in shadows,

my exalted soul still calls to you.


You are the time that guides my hours,

you are the idea that attends my mind,

because in you is concentrated all that exists,

my passion, my hope, my poetry.


There is no song that can equal your accent

when you tell me of your love and rave,

revealing the faith of your contentment;


I tremble at your voice and tremble if you look at me,

and I would like to exhale my last breath

burning in the air you breathe.




1845

translation.title: How I Adore You!
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps Coronado's sonnet as a concentrated declaration of passionate devotion.
